territorial_scope.description: Applies to persons doing business in Colorado that develop or deploy high-risk AI systems, and to Colorado residents as consumers.

evidence.quote: A PERSON DOING BUSINESS IN THIS STATE THAT DEPLOYS A HIGH-RISK ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Colorado statute adding Part 17 on artificial intelligence to Article 1 of Title 6, C.R.S. From 1 February 2026, developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems making consequential decisions about Colorado consumers must use reasonable care against algorithmic discrimination, with documentation, disclosure and risk-management duties. The Attorney General enforces it.
summary.long: Adds Part 17 (sections 6-1-1701 to 6-1-1707) to Article 1 of Title 6, Colorado Revised Statutes, on artificial intelligence systems. High-risk AI systems are those that make, or are a substantial factor in making, consequential decisions about Colorado consumers in education, employment, financial or lending services, essential government services, health care, housing, insurance or legal services. From 1 February 2026, developers must use reasonable care against known or foreseeable algorithmic discrimination, provide deployers with documentation and publish a statement; deployers must use reasonable care, adopt a risk management program, complete impact assessments at least annually, notify consumers before consequential decisions, give explanations for adverse decisions, correction and appeal rights, and report discovered discrimination within 90 days. Deployers with fewer than 50 full-time equivalent employees that do not use their own data to train the system are exempt from several duties under conditions. Consumer-facing AI systems must disclose AI interaction unless obvious. Exemptions cover certain federally approved systems, insurers, banks and credit unions. The Attorney General has exclusive enforcement authority; violations are unfair trade practices, with an affirmative defense for cured violations and a rebuttable presumption of reasonable care. No private right of action is created. The Attorney General may adopt rules.

obligations.summary: Developer of a high-risk AI system must use reasonable care to protect consumers from known or reasonably foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination arising from intended and contracted uses. A rebuttable presumption of reasonable care applies only in Attorney General enforcement actions (6-1-1706).
obligations.conditional_on: system is a high-risk artificial intelligence system (6-1-1701(9))

evidence.quote: A DEVELOPER OF A HIGH-RISK ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM SHALL USE REASONABLE CARE TO PROTECT CONSUMERS FROM ANY KNOWN OR REASONABLY FORESEEABLE RISKS OF ALGORITHMIC DISCRIMINATION

obligations.summary: Developer must make available to deployers or other developers: a general statement of foreseeable and harmful uses; documentation on training data types, limitations, purpose, intended benefits, evaluation, data governance, outputs and human use and monitoring (2); impact-assessment information to enable deployers to complete their assessments (3); and a publicly available statement of high-risk system types and how algorithmic discrimination risks are managed, updated as necessary and within 90 days after an intentional and substantial modification (4). Trade secrets and security-sensitive information need not be disclosed (6).
obligations.conditional_on: system is a high-risk artificial intelligence system

evidence.quote: A DEVELOPER OF A HIGH-RISK ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM SHALL MAKE AVAILABLE TO THE DEPLOYER OR OTHER DEVELOPER OF THE HIGH-RISK ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM

obligations.summary: Developer must disclose to the Attorney General, in a prescribed form, and to all known deployers or other developers, known or reasonably foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination without unreasonable delay and no later than 90 days after discovering, through its testing, that the system has caused or is reasonably likely to have caused algorithmic discrimination, or after receiving a credible deployer report of such discrimination.
obligations.conditional_on: developer discovers or receives a credible report that the high-risk system has caused algorithmic discrimination

evidence.quote: A DEVELOPER OF A HIGH-RISK ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM SHALL DISCLOSE TO THE ATTORNEY GENERAL, IN A FORM AND MANNER PRESCRIBED BY THE ATTORNEY GENERAL

obligations.summary: On the Attorney General's request, developer must disclose the statement or documentation described in 6-1-1702(2) no later than 90 days after the request, in the prescribed form. Developer may designate proprietary or trade-secret content, and privileged content is not waived.

evidence.quote: THE ATTORNEY GENERAL MAY REQUIRE THAT A DEVELOPER DISCLOSE TO THE ATTORNEY GENERAL, NO LATER THAN NINETY DAYS AFTER THE REQUEST

obligations.summary: Deployer of a high-risk system must use reasonable care to protect consumers from known or reasonably foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination. A rebuttable presumption of reasonable care applies only in Attorney General enforcement actions (6-1-1706).
obligations.conditional_on: system is a high-risk artificial intelligence system (6-1-1701(9))

evidence.quote: A DEPLOYER OF A HIGH-RISK ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM SHALL USE REASONABLE CARE TO PROTECT CONSUMERS FROM ANY KNOWN OR REASONABLY FORESEEABLE RISKS OF ALGORITHMIC DISCRIMINATION

obligations.summary: Deployer must implement a risk management policy and program governing deployment, specifying principles, processes and personnel to identify, document and mitigate algorithmic discrimination risks. It must be iterative, regularly and systematically reviewed and updated, and reasonable considering listed factors including recognised frameworks, size and complexity, system scope and sensitivity of data. Exempt deployers are listed in (6).
obligations.conditional_on: system is a high-risk artificial intelligence system; not an exempt small deployer under 6-1-1703(6)

evidence.quote: A DEPLOYER OF A HIGH-RISK ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM SHALL IMPLEMENT A RISK MANAGEMENT POLICY AND PROGRAM

obligations.summary: Deployer, or a third party it contracts, must complete an impact assessment before deploying a high-risk system, at least annually, and within 90 days after an intentional and substantial modification. Assessment content is set out in (3)(b)-(c). Assessments may cover comparable systems (3)(d) and may satisfy other-law assessments if reasonably similar (3)(e). Annual review that the system does not cause algorithmic discrimination is required by (3)(g).
obligations.conditional_on: system is a high-risk artificial intelligence system; not an exempt small deployer under 6-1-1703(6)

evidence.quote: A DEPLOYER, OR A THIRD PARTY CONTRACTED BY THE DEPLOYER, THAT DEPLOYS A HIGH-RISK ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM ON OR AFTER FEBRUARY 1, 2026, SHALL COMPLETE AN IMPACT ASSESSMENT

obligations.summary: Deployer must maintain the most recently completed impact assessment, all records concerning each assessment, and all prior assessments for at least three years following final deployment of the system.
obligations.conditional_on: system is a high-risk artificial intelligence system

evidence.quote: A DEPLOYER SHALL MAINTAIN THE MOST RECENTLY COMPLETED IMPACT ASSESSMENT FOR A HIGH-RISK ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM

obligations.summary: Before a consequential decision about a consumer is made, deployer must notify the consumer of the high-risk system's use, provide a statement of purpose, nature of the decision, deployer contact information, a plain-language description, and access instructions, and give information on any opt-out right under 6-1-1306 where applicable (4)(a). Notices must be given directly in plain language and in accessible formats, or otherwise made reasonably calculated to reach the consumer (4)(c). Where information is withheld, the consumer must be notified with a basis (8).
obligations.conditional_on: high-risk system is used to make or is a substantial factor in a consequential decision concerning a consumer

evidence.quote: THE DEPLOYER SHALL: (I) NOTIFY THE CONSUMER THAT THE DEPLOYER HAS DEPLOYED A HIGH-RISK ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM

obligations.summary: Where a consequential decision is adverse to the consumer, deployer must provide a statement of the principal reasons, including the degree and manner of the system's contribution, data types and data sources; an opportunity to correct incorrect personal data processed; and an opportunity to appeal, which must allow human review if technically feasible unless appeal is not in the consumer's best interest.
obligations.conditional_on: consequential decision concerning a consumer is adverse to the consumer

evidence.quote: IF THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION IS ADVERSE TO THE CONSUMER, PROVIDE TO THE CONSUMER

obligations.summary: Deployer must make available on its website a statement summarising the high-risk system types it deploys, how it manages algorithmic discrimination risks for each, and in detail the nature, source and extent of information it collects and uses; the statement must be periodically updated. Subject to the exemption in (6).
obligations.conditional_on: system is a high-risk artificial intelligence system; not an exempt small deployer under 6-1-1703(6)

evidence.quote: A DEPLOYER SHALL MAKE AVAILABLE, IN A MANNER THAT IS CLEAR AND READILY AVAILABLE ON THE DEPLOYER'S WEBSITE, A STATEMENT SUMMARIZING

obligations.summary: After discovering that a high-risk system has caused algorithmic discrimination, deployer must send a notice disclosing the discovery to the Attorney General without unreasonable delay and no later than 90 days after discovery, in the prescribed form.
obligations.conditional_on: deployer discovers that a high-risk system deployed on or after February 1, 2026 has caused algorithmic discrimination

evidence.quote: SHALL SEND TO THE ATTORNEY GENERAL, IN A FORM AND MANNER PRESCRIBED BY THE ATTORNEY GENERAL, A NOTICE DISCLOSING THE DISCOVERY

obligations.summary: On the Attorney General's request, deployer, or a third party it contracts, must disclose the risk management policy, impact assessment or records within 90 days after the request, in the prescribed form. Trade secrets may be designated and privileged content is not waived.

evidence.quote: THE ATTORNEY GENERAL MAY REQUIRE THAT A DEPLOYER, OR A THIRD PARTY CONTRACTED BY THE DEPLOYER, DISCLOSE TO THE ATTORNEY GENERAL

obligations.summary: Deployer or other developer that makes available an AI system intended to interact with consumers must ensure each consumer interacting with it is told that they are interacting with an AI system. Not required where it would be obvious to a reasonable person.
obligations.conditional_on: system is intended to interact with consumers and disclosure is not obvious to a reasonable person (6-1-1704(2))

evidence.quote: SHALL ENSURE THE DISCLOSURE TO EACH CONSUMER WHO INTERACTS WITH THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM

obligations.summary: Attorney General may promulgate rules needed to implement and enforce Part 17, including documentation requirements, notice contents, risk management and impact assessment content, the requirements for rebuttable presumptions and affirmative defences, and the process for recognising other risk management frameworks.

evidence.quote: THE ATTORNEY GENERAL MAY PROMULGATE RULES AS NECESSARY FOR THE PURPOSE OF IMPLEMENTING AND ENFORCING THIS PART 17

enforcement.triggered_by: Violation of the requirements established in Part 17 of Article 1 of Title 6 (6-1-1701 to 6-1-1707), treated as an unfair trade practice under 6-1-105(1)(hhhh)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Not stated in this text. The text makes a violation an unfair trade practice under 6-1-105(1)(hhhh) and does not state a penalty amount.
enforcement.penalty_reference: C.R.S. 6-1-105(1)(hhhh) (unfair trade practice; the penalty provisions are not reproduced in this text)
enforcement.cure_period: No fixed cure period stated. Section 6-1-1706(3) provides an affirmative defense for a developer, deployer or other person that discovers and cures a violation through feedback, adversarial testing or red teaming, or an internal review process, and is otherwise in compliance with a recognized risk management framework; the defense applies only in an Attorney General action.

evidence.quote: A VIOLATION OF THE REQUIREMENTS ESTABLISHED IN THIS PART 17 CONSTITUTES AN UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICE PURSUANT TO SECTION 6-1-105 (1)(hhhh).
